points.title: 童年启蒙
points.description: 达尔文出生于英格兰什鲁斯伯里一个富裕的医生家庭。他的祖父伊拉斯谟·达尔文是著名医生和博物学家，父亲罗伯特·达尔文也是当地知名医生。童年时期，达尔文对自然表现出浓厚兴趣，经常收集昆虫、矿物和鸟类标本。在什鲁斯伯里学校接受教育期间，他对传统课程不感兴趣，但对狩猎、骑马和自然科学探索充满热情。这段经历培养了他对自然细致观察的能力，为他后来的科学研究奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: Born in Shrewsbury, England to a wealthy family of physicians, Darwin showed early interest in natural history. His grandfather Erasmus Darwin was a prominent physician and naturalist, and his father Robert was a respected local doctor. During his childhood, Darwin collected specimens of insects, minerals, and birds. At Shrewsbury School, he struggled with traditional academics but excelled in outdoor activities like hunting, riding, and exploring nature. These formative years developed his keen observational skills that would later prove crucial for his scientific work.

points.title: 医学启蒙
points.description: 1825年，达尔文进入爱丁堡大学医学院学习医学，希望继承家族传统。然而，他对手术室的血腥场面感到极度不适，对医学课程也缺乏兴趣。在爱丁堡期间，他加入了普林尼学会，这是一个学生自然科学社团，在这里他结识了多位博物学家，并开始学习鸟类标本制作技术。他还参与了罗伯特·格兰特的海洋无脊椎动物研究，这进一步激发了他对自然科学的热情。这段经历使他意识到自己不适合医学事业，而是对生物学研究更感兴趣。
points.descriptionEn: In 1825, Darwin entered the University of Edinburgh Medical School to follow his family tradition. However, he was repulsed by the brutality of surgery and found medical lectures uninspiring. During his time in Edinburgh, he joined the Plinian Society, a student natural history society, where he met several naturalists and learned taxidermy skills. He also assisted Robert Grant in his research on marine invertebrates, further fueling his passion for natural science. This period convinced him that medicine was not his calling, and his interests lay in biological research.

points.title: 环球考察
points.description: 1831年，达尔文以博物学家身份登上英国皇家海军'小猎犬号'，开始了为期五年的环球航行。这次航行的目的地是南美洲海岸，但途中在加拉帕戈斯群岛停留时，达尔文观察到了不同岛屿上地雀的喙部形状差异，这些差异与各岛的食物来源密切相关。这一发现成为他后来提出自然选择理论的关键证据。在航行期间，他还收集了大量地质和生物标本，考察了南美洲的地质结构，并提出了珊瑚礁形成的理论。这次环球考察彻底改变了达尔文的人生轨迹，使他从一个业余博物学家转变为专业科学家，并为他后来的进化论研究积累了宝贵的第一手资料。
points.descriptionEn: In 1831, Darwin boarded HMS Beagle as a naturalist for a five-year voyage around the world. The expedition's primary destination was the South American coast, but a crucial stop at the Galápagos Islands proved pivotal. There, Darwin observed variations in the beak shapes of finches across different islands, which correlated with their food sources. This observation became key evidence for his later theory of natural selection. During the voyage, he collected extensive geological and biological specimens, studied South American geology, and developed his theory of coral reef formation. This journey transformed Darwin from an amateur naturalist to a professional scientist and provided the firsthand data that would fuel his evolutionary research.

points.title: 理论构建
points.description: 1842年，达尔文与妻子艾玛移居伦敦郊外的唐恩村，并在那里度过了余生。在唐恩村，达尔文开始系统地整理和分析他在环球考察中收集的资料，并逐渐形成了进化论的核心思想。他进行了大量的植物实验，特别是对藤本植物的研究，并撰写了关于珊瑚礁、火山活动和地质学的著作。这一时期，达尔文还与多位科学家保持通信交流，包括著名的植物学家约瑟夫·胡克和地质学家查尔斯·莱尔。1858年，当阿尔弗雷德·拉塞尔·华莱士提出了与达尔文相似的进化理论时，两人共同发表了关于自然选择的论文。1859年，达尔文出版了《物种起源》，这部著作系统地阐述了自然选择理论，彻底改变了人类对生命起源和发展的认识。
points.descriptionEn: In 1842, Darwin moved with his wife Emma to Downe, a village in the London suburbs, where he would spend the rest of his life. In Downe, Darwin began systematically organizing and analyzing the data from his voyage, gradually developing the core ideas of his theory of evolution. He conducted extensive botanical experiments, particularly on climbing plants, and wrote works on coral reefs, volcanic activity, and geology. During this period, he maintained correspondence with scientists including botanist Joseph Hooker and geologist Charles Lyell. In 1858, when Alfred Russel Wallace independently developed a similar theory of evolution, Darwin and Wallace jointly presented papers on natural selection. In 1859, Darwin published 'On the Origin of Species,' which systematically presented his theory of natural selection and revolutionized humanity's understanding of life's origins and development.

points.title: 晚年成就
points.description: 1860年后，达尔文虽然健康状况不佳，但仍然保持高产的研究和写作。他继续完善进化论，出版了《人类的由来及性选择》(1871)，将进化理论应用于人类，提出了人类与非洲猿类有共同祖先的观点。他还研究了植物的运动和感知能力，以及植物异花受精和自花受精的后果。达尔文晚年获得了多项荣誉，包括1878年被授予皇家学会科普利奖章。1882年4月19日，达尔文在伦敦逝世，享年73岁。他被安葬在威斯敏斯特大教堂，紧挨着另一位科学巨匠艾萨克·牛顿。达尔文的进化论不仅改变了生物学，也对哲学、宗教和社会科学产生了深远影响，成为现代科学的基础理论之一。
points.descriptionEn: After 1860, despite poor health, Darwin remained highly productive in research and writing. He continued to develop his theory of evolution, publishing 'The Descent of Man, and Selection in Relation to Sex' (1871), which applied evolutionary theory to humans and proposed that humans shared a common ancestor with African apes. He also studied plant movements and sensory abilities, as well as the consequences of cross- and self-fertilization in plants. In his later years, Darwin received numerous honors, including the Royal Society's Copley Medal in 1878. On April 19, 1882, Darwin died in London at the age of 73. He was buried in Westminster Abbey, near fellow scientific giant Isaac Newton. Darwin's theory of evolution not only transformed biology but also had profound impacts on philosophy, religion, and social sciences, becoming one of the foundational theories of modern science.

supporter.zh: 达尔文被誉为现代生物学之父，他的进化论彻底改变了人类对生命世界的认识。支持者认为，达尔文的理论不仅具有科学革命性，还体现了科学方法的精髓——基于观察、实验和推理。他的自然选择理论为理解生物多样性、适应性以及物种形成提供了统一框架，至今仍是生物学的核心理论。达尔文的研究精神和对真理的追求，激励了后世无数科学家，他的著作《物种起源》被公认为科学史上最具影响力的著作之一。
supporter.en: Darwin is hailed as the father of modern biology, and his theory of evolution revolutionized humanity's understanding of the living world. Supporters argue that his work represents not just a scientific revolution but embodies the essence of the scientific method—based on observation, experimentation, and reasoning. His theory of natural selection provides a unifying framework for understanding biodiversity, adaptation, and speciation, remaining central to biology today. Darwin's spirit of inquiry and pursuit of truth has inspired countless scientists throughout history, and 'On the Origin of Species' is recognized as one of the most influential scientific works ever published.

critic.zh: 批评者指出，达尔文的进化论存在诸多局限性。首先，他缺乏对遗传机制的理解，孟德尔的遗传定律直到他去世后才被重新发现并整合到进化论中。其次，达尔文过度依赖渐变进化，难以解释化石记录中的'间断平衡'现象。此外，他的理论被一些人滥用，为种族主义和社会达尔文主义提供了'科学'依据。批评者还认为，达尔文对人类进化的解释过于简化，忽视了文化、社会因素在人类发展中的重要作用。这些批评反映了科学理论的历史局限性，也提醒我们科学知识总是在不断修正和完善中。
critic.en: Critics point out several limitations in Darwin's theory of evolution. First, he lacked understanding of genetic mechanisms, as Mendel's laws of inheritance were only rediscovered and integrated into evolutionary theory after his death. Second, Darwin's emphasis on gradual evolution struggled to explain the 'punctuated equilibrium' observed in the fossil record. Additionally, his theory was sometimes misused to provide 'scientific' justification for racism and social Darwinism. Critics also argue that Darwin's explanation of human evolution was overly simplistic, neglecting the important roles of culture and society in human development. These criticisms reflect the historical limitations of scientific theories and remind us that scientific knowledge is constantly being revised and refined.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，达尔文被塑造为科学革命的象征人物。他的形象超越了单纯的科学家，成为理性思维与宗教信仰冲突的代表性人物。达尔文与牛津主教威尔伯福斯著名的辩论，以及'猴子审判'等事件，使他成为科学与宗教论战的标志性人物。在流行文化中，达尔文常被描绘为孤独的天才，与疾病斗争的勇者，以及挑战传统权威的思想先锋。他的进化论不仅改变了科学，也深刻影响了哲学、文学和艺术，成为现代性的重要组成部分。达尔文的形象体现了科学探索的艰辛与伟大，以及人类不断突破认知边界的永恒追求。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Darwin has been portrayed as a symbolic figure of scientific revolution. His image transcends that of a mere scientist, becoming representative of the conflict between rational thought and religious belief. The famous debate between Darwin and Bishop Wilberforce at Oxford, along with events like the 'Scopes Monkey Trial,' have made him an iconic figure in the science-religion controversy. In popular culture, Darwin is often depicted as a lonely genius, a hero battling illness, and a thought pioneer challenging traditional authority. His theory of evolution not only transformed science but also profoundly influenced philosophy, literature, and art, becoming an essential component of modernity. Darwin's image embodies the hardships and greatness of scientific exploration and humanity's perpetual quest to transcend cognitive boundaries.

self.zh: 能够生存下来的不是最强的物种，也不是最聪明的物种，而是最能适应变化的物种。
self.en: It is not the strongest of the species that survives, nor the most intelligent that survives. It is the one that is most adaptable to change.

others.zh: 达尔文的著作是生物学史上最伟大的成就之一，它彻底改变了我们对自己在自然界中位置的理解。
others.en: Darwin's work is one of the greatest achievements in the history of biology, which completely changed our understanding of our place in the natural world.
